title: Accounts Administrator
description:
Job Title: Accounts Administrator
Location: Studley
Salary: £28,000-£32,000 per annum, depending on experience
Hours: Full-time
I'm working with an established business based in Studley who are looking to recruit an organised and hands-on Accounts Administrator to join their team.
This is a varied role offering genuine responsibility, working closely with colleagues across the business and an external accountant. You'll play an important part in keeping the day-to-day finance function running smoothly, maintaining accurate records and ensuring customer payments are followed up.
If you enjoy working in a varied finance role where you can take ownership, use your initiative and make a real contribution, this could be an excellent opportunity.
Key responsibilities:
- Processing day-to-day financial transactions accurately using Xero.
- Completing bank and account reconciliations and investigating discrepancies.
- Monitoring outstanding customer invoices and proactively chasing overdue payments by telephone and email.
- Allocating customer payments and maintaining accurate sales ledger records.
- Reviewing aged debt reports and escalating overdue accounts where necessary.
- Processing supplier invoices, checking documentation and preparing payments.
- Allocating transactions to the correct cost centres.
- Liaising with customers, suppliers and the external accountant.
- Maintaining accurate financial records and supporting month-end and year-end activities.
- Assisting with compliance records, financial documentation and general accounts administration.
- Identifying opportunities to improve processes and support the wider business.

About you
You'll be a practical, reliable and detail-focused finance professional who enjoys taking responsibility for your work.
Ideally, you'll have:
- Previous experience in accounts administration, accounts assistance, bookkeeping or credit control.
- Experience using Xero or another accounting package.
- A good understanding of purchase ledger, sales ledger and reconciliations.
- Confidence chasing outstanding payments and having professional conversations about money owed.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to manage your workload independently and meet deadlines.
- Good communication skills and a proactive approach.
- A relevant qualification such as AAT would be beneficial but is not essential.

What's on offer?
- Salary of £28,000-£32,000, depending on experience.
- Full-time, permanent employment.
- A varied role with genuine responsibility and ownership.
- A supportive working environment.
- The opportunity to develop your skills and contribute to improving finance processes.

Interested?
If you're looking for a hands-on accounts role where you can make a difference and become a valued member of the team, I'd love to hear from you.

title: Group Credit Controller
description:
- Group Credit Controller
- Permanent, full-time
- Up to £45k, own the group credit policy

Group Credit Controller
This is a chance to own credit control for a whole group, not just a single ledger. You will look after customers across multiple countries and currencies, with a real say over credit limits, terms and how the business protects its cash. The business is growing quickly, and the role has genuine scope to grow with it.
You are an experienced credit controller who is as comfortable making a judgement call on a credit limit as you are picking up the phone to chase an invoice. You know when to flex for a good customer and when to raise the alarm. You like working closely with sales teams, and you want to improve the numbers, not just report on them.

What You Will Be Doing
- Owning credit risk and collections across an international customer base, prioritising by value, age and risk so your time goes where it counts
- Driving debtor days and overdue debt down with clear targets and actions, rather than just reporting where they sit
- Assessing new and existing customers using credit reference data, trade references, payment history and management accounts, and forming a clear, evidenced view of the risk
- Making and recommending credit limits and terms, flexing pragmatically when there is a genuine commercial case
- Acting as a trusted adviser to sales leaders and sales operations, including calls on whether to release or hold orders for customers who are over limit
- Managing the credit insurance policies, from limit applications and maximising cover to being the main contact for brokers and insurers
- Running customer rebates from start to finish: recording agreements, then calculating, accruing and settling them accurately
- Resolving deductions, disputes and under or over payments, and working with sales and operations to fix the root cause rather than the symptom
- Producing the customer receipts forecast for each entity, preparing bad and doubtful debt provisions and delivering KPI reporting with clear commentary for non-finance readers
- Writing and maintaining the group credit policy, leading automation of credit and AR processes, and supporting month end, reconciliations and audit on the receivables side

What We Need From You
- Someone with solid, hands-on credit control experience who has done the whole job: risk assessment, collections and dispute resolution, not just chasing overdue invoices
- A person with good commercial judgement who is confident enough to flex a limit when it is justified and to escalate when it is not
- Someone who has managed credit across international markets, with multi-currency ledgers and differing payment practices, and who adapts their approach to local context
- A track record of bringing debtor days and overdue debt down that you can talk through with real numbers
- Comfortable with credit reference agencies and reading customer management accounts and financial statements to judge whether a customer is a safe bet
- Experience of credit insurance (limits, claims, renewals), and ideally some exposure to managing rebates or similar commercial agreements
- Advanced Excel, experience of an ERP system and a genuine curiosity about how automation and AI tools could improve credit and AR processes
- A confident communicator who can advise and influence at every level, firm when it is needed and warm with it, because customers expect a premium experience

What's in it for you
- A salary of up to £45,000 per annum
- A permanent, full-time role in a business that is growing fast
- Real ownership: you will shape the group credit policy rather than inherit someone else's
- Genuine scope to grow as the group develops
- A varied customer base across several markets and time zones, so no two days look the same
- Close working relationships with regional sales leaders rather than being tucked away in the corner of the finance team
- The chance to lead the automation and improvement of credit and AR processes

If this sounds like the credit control role you have been looking for and you tick most of these boxes, we would love to hear from you.

This position would suit an experienced payroll professional who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, has excellent attention to detail and takes pride in delivering an accurate and efficient payroll service. Experience within construction, engineering or related sectors would be particularly beneficial.

The Role

As Payroll Administrator, you will play a key role in managing weekly and monthly payroll activities, maintaining payroll records and supporting employees with payroll-related queries. You will work closely with both finance and HR colleagues to ensure payroll processes run smoothly and efficiently.

Key Responsibilities
- Process weekly and monthly payrolls accurately and within set deadlines.
- Maintain employee payroll records, including starters, leavers and contractual changes.
- Review and process timesheets, overtime, holiday pay and payroll adjustments.
- Administer statutory payments and deductions in line with current legislation.
- Complete payroll reconciliations and support month-end reporting requirements.
- Prepare and submit payroll information to HMRC.
- Process employee expenses and ensure compliance with company policies.
- Manage pension contributions and payroll deductions.
- Respond to employee payroll queries and resolve discrepancies in a timely manner.
- Assist with payroll reporting and wider finance administration when required.
- Maintain confidentiality of payroll data and employee information at all times.

About You

It is a mandatory requirement that the successful candidate has previous payroll experience together with a strong understanding of payroll procedures and legislation. You will be highly organised, comfortable working to deadlines and able to manage a varied workload with minimal supervision. Experience of CIS (Construction Industry Scheme) would be highly advantageous.

Skills & Experience Required
- Strong understanding of payroll legislation and HMRC requirements.
- Experience processing payroll from start to finish.
- Excellent numerical and administrative skills.
- Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to work.
- Effective communication skills with the ability to build positive working relationships.
- Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

Desirable Experience
- Experience using Sage Payroll and/or COINS software.
- Knowledge of CIS (Construction Industry Scheme) regulations and payroll processes.
- Experience of working within construction, engineering or contracting environments.

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary.
- Supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Varied role with broad payroll responsibilities.
- Opportunity to join a stable and growing organisation.
- Ongoing training and development opportunities.

If you are an experienced Payroll Administrator looking to join a well-established business where you can make a genuine contribution, we would welcome your application.

This role is full time, office based.

Experience working with a diverse workforce, including teaching staff, academic professionals, administrators, and support personnel, would be particularly valuable.

Essential Qualifications & Experience

- Experience supporting payroll audits and compliance reviews.
- Experience improving payroll processes or implementing payroll systems.
